name: Cian Malik
life: “I still remember shorthand drawn in the flour on a worktop.” Friday often includes a stop at the crossing outside Verve Nail Studio, where Cian notices whose chair is empty and who has stayed talking after an appointment.
voice: I recognized my first boss's pencil shorthand. I can read the tab nobody else understands.
appearance: Cian has black hair twisted into a small knot, a wide brow and a narrow jaw, and a favorite piece of clothing, a moss-green cardigan. It usually goes with a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case. When somebody else has the floor, Cian squares up pieces of paper while thinking.
personality: Cian has a long memory for unfair prices and a short one for small insults. Cian can get along perfectly well with an enemy provided the account between them is clear.
agenda: To read the shorthand on the oldest tab.
family: Malcolm Tan is Cian’s second cousin. Cian asks before bringing somebody along. Malcolm can always ask for five minutes alone. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The fountain score*, Malcolm says, “I brought an empty milk tin from the shop my parents lost.”
connections: Duncan Griffin. An old shorthand entry and a foreign coin give the fault a history.

reactions.situation: A customer cannot pay until the till opens
reactions.response: Cian asks the cashier what can safely go on a temporary tab.

reactions.situation: A frightened child is waiting outside a shuttered shop
reactions.response: Cian stays where the child can see the shop door and asks the neighboring counter to help find the adult expected there.
